text.text_excerpt: We came to St. Roch for dinner and I wanted something light so I ordered the rainbow quinoa salad. It was really great. The almonds in the quinoa really make that dish if you ask me. I also got the skinny smoothie that was pretty good. The price was a little steep, but I feel like that's a normal occurrence for healthy food AND food at St. Roch. The only reason they are getting 4 stars instead of 5 is the service. It was pretty lackluster. I don't know if the two people working were just tired or what, but I did not feel very welcome walking up to the counter. I'd go back there the next visit to St. Roch for sure, but I would hope the vendors would be in a better mood.

Two words: AVOCADO TOAST! It was our last day in New Orleans, and we felt soooooo FAT and bloated from all the rich and delicious food we ate throughout our whole trip, we decided to make the trek to St. Roch's Market for some "lighter" options. Juice NOLA was the first vendor I saw walking in, and at quick glance the only words I saw were: "juice", "avocado", "quinoa". I immediately decided I was going to grab a late breakfast there. I decided to go with the avocado toast with an added fried egg because I love avocado and it looked to be one of the smaller options for food. The Rainbow Bowl looked rather large, and let's be honest, I was nursing a slight hangover, so that much food didn'...

This is a cool spot in the St. Roch Market. They have a variety of salads, grain bowls, juices and smoothies. The staff are very friendly and do a great job. We used to get some of their grain bowls to split, but lately we have been hooked on their Avocado Toast. I think it's the best I have had from anywhere. They get their bread from the local Bellegarde Bakery. It's delicious. It's a thick country loaf that toasts quite nicely. They also offer it with an egg on top, but I prefer it without the egg. We typically get this every Sunday, so I know we will be back.
